newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - UK stocks seen sluggish over two years.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - UK stocks seen sluggish over two years.

text.p: British stocks could end 1997 little changed from current levels as political jitters and expectations of higher interest rates take their toll on the market, a Reuters survey of forecasts from equity analysts showed on Wednesday.
An average of forecasts from 13 London-based analysts predicted the FTSE-100 index would end this year at around 4,400 points, barely changed from a March 13 close of 4,397.7.
Stocks may fare slightly better next year but there will be no surge. Eight analysts put the FTSE at around 4,625 at the end of 1998.

Prime Minister and Conservative party leader John Major has called a general election for May 1. Opposition Labour, streets ahead in the polls, are widely expected to win, and this may cause wobbles in the stock market.
"The FTSE is going down because the Conservatives are going to lose the election. The equity market will react badly."
KEVIN GARDINER, UK ECONOMIST, MORGAN STANLEY.

"There is ... the possibility of a change in taxation with a Labour government. In particular I'd be looking at the possibility of a change in dividend taxation and possibly even a change in corporate taxation."
RICHARD JEFFREY, GROUP ECONOMIST AT CHARTERHOUSE.

"Interest rates are going to go up sharply. There may be a lull in domestic demand at the moment, but the second half of this year will be much more active and the government will have to react with higher interest rates."
